chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Your blood is cleaner than the blood of someone else. When it is in your garment like a splatter of your own blood, there is no problem, and if it is the blood of someone else, whether little or much, then wash it.

key_terms.دَمُكَ: Your blood (referring to the person praying)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem (it is pure)

ai.seo_question: Is a person's own blood considered pure or impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential distinction between one's own blood, deemed pure (tahir) and excusable in small quantities, and the blood of others, which is impure (najis) and requires washing regardless of volume. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the ontological purity of self-blood versus the impurity of foreign blood, providing practical guidance for maintaining ritual validity during prayer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Your blood is cleaner than the blood of someone else. When it was in your clothes, like a drop from you own blood, so there is no problem, and if it was the blood of someone else, whether it was little or more, so wash it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said

that your blood to you is less unclean than other people’s blood. If you find like sprinkles of your blood on you, it is not harmful; but if it is other people’s blood, regardless of its being of a small or large quantity, you must wash it clean.’”
